newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party joins chorus in attacking poll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party joins chorus in attacking poll.

text.p: The fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), whose share of the vote plunged in last week's general elections, said on Wednesday there had been irregularities in the poll.

The vote share of the Christian-Nationalist PDI, one of only three parties legally permitted to contest the elections held every five years, plummeted to three percent from 15 percent in the last poll in 1992.

"Various irregularities took place during the election campaign, the cooling-off period, vote casting and vote counting," the party said in a statement issued after a meeting of senior party officials.
"The PDI will decide whether it will join the next stages of the elections if the (irregularities) are not handled properly by the election organiser," it said.
It did not give further details and PDI officials could not be reached for comment.

The ruling Golkar, in power for most of President Suharto's 30-year rule, swept the poll with more than 74 percent of the national vote. The other legal party, the Moslem-backed United Development Party (PPP), won just under 23 percent.
The PPP has also complained of electoral irregularities and its leaders were due to meet on Thursday to decide whether to accept the result.

The campaign saw the worst political violence in Indonesia in three decades, primarily between supporters of the PPP and Golkar. Financial markets were watching the outcome of the PPP meeting for fear of further violence.

The PDI, badly split by a leadership battle, also saw the number of its members drop to 10 from 56 in the 500-seat House of Representatives. It said on Tuesday it was considering withdrawing from parliament, whose rules require each party to provide an individual representative to each of the 11 commissions.
Political analysts said, however, the government might seek a way around this numbers problem, possibly through a change in parliamentary rules.
